text_en: 1. The Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy of the Republic of Moldova 2023-2030 (hereinafter the Programme) is approved (annexed).
summary: The draft Government Decision approves the Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030.
extraction_note: Draft decision as tabled for the Government meeting of 28 May 2025 (number and date blank); recorded as proposed on the wording of the draft. The source register notes the Government approved it on that date (press release), which this text does not state.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 2.2. [The responsible authorities and institutions] will submit annually, by 25 February, to the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation, and on request, reports on the implementation of the Action Plan.
summary: Responsible institutions will report annually to the Ministry, by 25 February, on implementing the Action Plan.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 3. The Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation will submit to the Government annually, by 1 April, the generalised progress report on the implementation of the Programme.
summary: The Ministry will give the Government an annual generalised progress report on the Programme by 1 April.
extraction_note: Annual reporting by 1 April also at page 75 (Notă de fundamentare), not extracted again.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 1. The Implementation Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Transformation Strategy of the Republic of Moldova 2023-2030 is a medium-term (3-year) public policy document, drawn up to implement the general objectives set by the Strategy approved by Government Decision No. 650/2023 (STDM), and proposes an action plan to consolidate a resilient digital economy aligned with the European Union model, modernise the government digital infrastructure, increase digital literacy and the acceptance of ICT products, etc.
summary: The Programme implements the 2023-2030 Strategy with a three-year action plan for an EU-aligned digital economy and modernised government digital infrastructure.
extraction_note: Digital literacy, also named in the sentence, is not a theme area. Restated in the Notă de fundamentare (pages 67), not extracted again.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 3. At the same time, the Programme contributes to approximating Moldova's national legislation to EU legal acts, under Article 102, Chapter 18 'Information society' of the Association Agreement between the Republic of Moldova and the European Union, ratified by Law 112/2014, and to the international instruments listed in Annex XXVIIIB of the Association Agreement.
summary: The Programme contributes to approximating national law to EU acts under the Association Agreement chapter on information society.
extraction_note: Chapter 18 is a chapter of the Association Agreement, not an accession chapter; cluster and chapter left empty. Repeated in the Notă de fundamentare (page 67), not extracted again.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 9. Last but not least, the Programme is aligned with and complementary to the Moldova Growth Plan, with a focus on integration into the Digital Single Market and transposition of and harmonisation with key EU legislation, standards and norms.
summary: The Programme is aligned with the Moldova Growth Plan, focusing on Digital Single Market integration and transposing key EU digital legislation.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 14. The Programme was drawn up through an inclusive and dynamic process, its content and actions being discussed and validated at meetings of the National Council for Digitalisation established by Order No. 165/2023 of the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation, and of the sector council on external assistance for the sectors coordinated by the Ministry, established by Order No. 60 of 20 May 2024, whose members are representatives of the institutions responsible for implementing the Programme's actions, academia and business associations in the sector.
summary: The Programme was validated in the National Council for Digitalisation, set up by ministerial Order 165/2023, and an external assistance sector council.
extraction_note: M2: the establishment of the National Council for Digitalisation by order is recorded as an adopted intervention. The next sentence (consultation with the EU Delegation and EU4Digital experts) is not extracted separately.
intervention_as_stated: Consiliul Național pentru Digitalizare (Ordinul MDED nr. 165/2023)

text_en: 15. According to the digital transformation readiness assessment of Moldova carried out by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 2021, Moldova obtained 4.1 points out of 5, placing it at the differentiation stage, the fourth of five stages of readiness for digital transformation.
summary: UNDP's 2021 digital readiness assessment scored Moldova 4.1 of 5, the fourth of five readiness stages.
extraction_note: Same assessment also at page 68 (Notă de fundamentare), not extracted again. The sub-scores in the same paragraph concern digital literacy and are not extracted.

text_en: In 2024, 39.4% of citizens say they can use electronic services independently, 33.7% need occasional help and 24.8% prefer to delegate the obtaining of a service entirely.
summary: In 2024, 39.4% of citizens could use e-services independently, 33.7% needed occasional help and 24.8% delegated entirely.
extraction_note: The Notă de fundamentare (page 68) gives 40.5% able to use e-services independently; extracted there because the figure differs.

text_en: In the first three quarters of 2024, 80.3% of requests for G2B services were made online and only 19.7% are still made at counters. G2C services, however, show moderate adoption: only 41% of total requests.
summary: In the first three quarters of 2024, 80.3% of business service requests were online, against 41% for citizen services.

text_en: Young people aged 18 to 29 are the most active users of electronic services, using them three times more often than people aged 60-74.
summary: People aged 18-29 use electronic services three times more often than those aged 60-74.

text_en: These discrepancies indicate an urgent need to reduce the digital divide and ensure access to electronic services for all categories of the population.
summary: Age and education gaps in e-service use show an urgent need to reduce the digital divide in access to e-services.

text_en: Interest in online public services peaked in 2024, with 47.4% of respondents using the internet to obtain information about medical services. In 2024, 40% of respondents said they had searched online for information about government organisations. There was also an increase in interest in information about cultural institutions (33.4%) and in requesting public services online (26.6%).
summary: In 2024, 40% of respondents searched online for government information and 26.6% requested public services online.

text_en: 2) Access to computers is higher in urban areas (67%) than in rural areas (41%), and this remains a major challenge that deepens the digital divide.
summary: AGE 2024 survey: 67% of urban households have computers against 41% in rural areas, deepening the digital divide.
extraction_note: From the 2024 national survey of the e-Governance Agency (para. 20). Device ownership as part of the digital divide; doubtful whether it meets the materiality test for connectivity (TECH-INFRA). The age and education items of the same list are not extracted separately.

text_en: 4) There is a significant difference between high-income (72.4%) and low-income (23.4%) households in computer ownership. This indicator has fallen since 2022, when 40% of low-income households reported owning a computer, owing to the shift to various types of mobile devices.
summary: Computer ownership is 72.4% in high-income and 23.4% in low-income households, down from 40% in 2022.
extraction_note: AGE 2024 survey; device ownership, theme doubtful as for the previous item.

text_en: 21. According to the Speedtest Global Index, which compares monthly internet access speed data for 100 countries, the Republic of Moldova ranks 57th for mobile broadband speed (download speed 50 Mbps, against a global average of 48 Mbps) and fortieth for fixed broadband speed (download speed 122 Mbps, above the global average of 98 Mbps).
summary: Speedtest Global Index: Moldova 57th for mobile broadband (50 Mbps) and 40th for fixed broadband (122 Mbps).
extraction_note: The Notă de fundamentare (page 68) gives fixed broadband speed of 106 Mbps; extracted there because it differs.

text_en: 22. Moldova is among the world leaders in the affordability of Gigabit internet for the population, over 90%, at affordable tariffs, which is an important advantage for developing the digital economy.
summary: Moldova is among world leaders in Gigabit internet accessibility, over 90% of the population at affordable tariffs.

text_en: Combined with 98% 4G coverage and significant penetration of optical fibre, users have a wide range of options, but this degree of availability of high-speed networks does not yet have the expected economic and social impact.
summary: Despite 98% 4G coverage and wide fibre, high-speed network availability does not yet have the expected economic and social impact.

text_en: 23. The total number of fixed broadband internet connections in the Republic of Moldova reached 825.2 thousand at the end of 2023, an increase of 4.6% on the third quarter of 2022 and of 25.9% on the third quarter of 2019, an increase of 169.5 thousand fixed internet subscribers.
summary: Fixed broadband connections reached 825,200 at end-2023, up 25.9% on the third quarter of 2019.

text_en: There was also a substantial increase in the number of mobile broadband internet customers, from 2.4 million in 2019 to 3.0 million at the end of 2023, an increase of 602.6 thousand.
summary: Mobile broadband customers rose from 2.4 million in 2019 to 3.0 million at end-2023.

text_en: Of a total of 1.1 million households, 825.2 thousand are connected to the internet, of which 747.5 thousand via optical fibre and 68.6 thousand via ADSL.
summary: Of 1.1 million households, 825,200 are connected to the internet, 747,500 of them by optical fibre.

text_en: 24. Based on analysis of data from fixed internet providers, there are 431 localities in the Republic of Moldova that fall within the definition of 'white areas'.
summary: Provider data show 431 localities in Moldova are broadband 'white areas'.

text_en: Most of these localities are small and isolated, requiring significant investment to extend the broadband internet network.
summary: Most white-area localities are small and isolated and need significant investment to extend broadband.

text_en: In total, there are about 72 thousand households in white-area localities, or 6.3% of all households in the country.
summary: About 72,000 households, 6.3% of all households, are in broadband white areas.

text_en: There is a direct correlation between the size of a locality and the chances that it lacks broadband internet.
summary: The smaller a locality, the more likely it lacks broadband internet.

text_en: Thus, 81.2% of respondents to the AGE survey said they access the internet via the mobile phone, up 3% on 2022 and 8% on 2021.
summary: 81.2% of AGE survey respondents access the internet by mobile phone, up 8% on 2021.

text_en: 26. Total traffic generated by mobile internet users in 2023 rose by about 25.9% or 67,341 TB on the previous year, of which smartphone users (voice users) generated traffic up about 35.6% or 71,891 TB, while dedicated mobile internet users consumed about 7.8% or 4,550 TB less, which clearly indicates users' device preferences
summary: Mobile internet traffic in 2023 rose about 25.9% (67,341 TB), driven by smartphone users.
extraction_note: The converted text reads '455 0 TB' for the dedicated mobile figure; translated as 4,550 TB. Source of the figure: ANRCETI (Figure 2).

text_en: 33. Health digitalisation is a growing priority for the Republic of Moldova, in the context of implementing the eRețeta system (over 270,000 reimbursed prescriptions issued monthly at the end of 2024) and of modernising digital platforms in the public medical sector. Currently, the SIA AMP information system is used by about 400 institutions and processes over 11 million consultations annually, including over 150,000 online appointments in 2024.
summary: eRețeta issues over 270,000 reimbursed e-prescriptions monthly; SIA AMP serves about 400 institutions, with over 150,000 online appointments in 2024.
extraction_note: eHealth online services (e-prescriptions, online appointments) counted as digital government under the materiality test. Paragraph also proposed by the Ministry of Health in the consultation synthesis (page 76), not extracted again.

text_en: However, the lack of a functional electronic health record, limited interoperability and the absence of a dedicated institutional framework remain major challenges.
summary: The lack of a functional electronic health record, limited interoperability and no dedicated institutional framework remain major eHealth challenges.

text_en: The Strategic Health Digitalisation Programme 2030, being drafted, provides for creating an integrated digital ecosystem coordinated by an entity dedicated to e-Health. It aims that, by 2030, over 50% of the insured population will have access to the Electronic Health Record, in line with the objectives of the Digital Transformation Strategy (STDM) and the standards of the European Health Data Space (EHDS).
summary: A Strategic Health Digitalisation Programme 2030 is being drafted: an e-Health entity and EHR access for over 50% of the insured by 2030.
extraction_note: in_progress on the wording 'aflat în curs de elaborare' (being drafted). The need for the programme is restated at page 27 (OS 1.4 rationale), not extracted again.
intervention_as_stated: Programul strategic de digitalizare a sănătății 2030

text_en: 34. The development of a digital society depends on the existence of an accessible digital identity widely adopted by citizens. In turn, the adoption of digital identity and electronic signature depends directly on the availability and use of electronic services that integrate these tools.
summary: Digital society depends on a widely adopted digital identity, whose adoption in turn depends on e-services that integrate it.

text_en: This condition was confirmed by the Information Technology and Cyber Security Service (STISC), which reported that demand for and use of the electronic signature service increased substantially when the Integrated Health Information System was implemented.
summary: STISC reported that demand for and use of electronic signatures rose substantially when the Integrated Health Information System was implemented.
extraction_note: STISC's statement as reported by the Programme. The same wording is proposed by STISC in the consultation synthesis (pages 81 and 133), not extracted again.

text_en: With only 10% of the population of the Republic of Moldova holding qualified certificates for electronic signature, genuine digital transformation remains a significant challenge.
summary: Only 10% of the population hold qualified electronic signature certificates.
extraction_note: Also at page 68 (Notă de fundamentare) and in STISC's proposal at pages 81 and 133, not extracted again.

text_en: This low adoption rate is all the more worrying since most current holders are public sector employees, obliged by the nature of their profession to use electronic signatures.
summary: Most current electronic signature holders are public sector employees obliged to use them.

text_en: According to data provided by STISC, on 30 September 2024 there were only 246,674 valid qualified certificates for electronic signature, including all types of electronic identification means (USB tokens, mobile IDs and electronic identity cards).
summary: STISC: 246,674 valid qualified electronic signature certificates on 30 September 2024, across all identification means.

text_en: The situation is even more critical in the diaspora, where in 2023 only 67 electronic signature certificates were issued in the 41 diplomatic missions and consular offices, showing the extremely limited accessibility of currently existing digital services for Moldovan citizens abroad.
summary: Only 67 electronic signature certificates were issued in 2023 across Moldova's 41 diplomatic missions and consular offices.
extraction_note: Diaspora access to e-services; not linked to Chapter 2 in the text, so theme only.

text_en: The low adoption of digital identity in the Republic of Moldova is the direct consequence of the limited accessibility of existing tools, combined with insufficient digitalisation of public services, which do not yet offer convincing benefits to justify the time and resources needed to obtain and use electronic identification means.
summary: Low digital identity adoption results from limited accessibility of tools and insufficiently digitalised public services lacking convincing benefits.
extraction_note: Restated in the author's responses in the consultation synthesis (pages 81, 84-85 and 134), with a wider list of factors at page 81; the wider list is extracted there.

text_en: To accelerate digital transformation and use available financial resources efficiently, the Government is to promptly prioritise the digitalisation and automation of public service delivery processes, as well as the implementation of a digital identity wallet.
summary: The Government is to prioritise digitalising and automating public service delivery and implementing a digital identity wallet.
extraction_note: The following sentences (preventing investment in unused services; digital identity as a strategic priority aligned with European e-governance standards) give the rationale and are not extracted separately.
intervention_as_stated: Programul de implementare, pentru anii 2025-2027, a Strategiei de transformare digitală a Republicii Moldova pentru anii 2023-2030

text_en: 35. The electronic identity card, being launched by ASP, is an important step in this direction. It will include an embedded qualified digital certificate for creating electronic signatures, allowing citizens to sign documents online with full legal value.
summary: The electronic identity card being launched by ASP will embed a qualified certificate for legally valid online signatures.
extraction_note: in_progress on 'în curs de lansare'. Related reported views on Law 68/2024 (page 111) and the 2025 launch (page 130) are extracted separately.
intervention_as_stated: Cartea de identitate electronică

text_en: In turn, institutions cooperate and reuse existing services; thus STISC together with ASP has extended the number of registration service providers so that qualified trust services are delivered through ASP offices throughout the country.
summary: STISC and ASP extended registration providers so qualified trust services are delivered through ASP offices nationwide.
extraction_note: Text proposed by STISC in the synthesis (page 134), not extracted again.
intervention_as_stated: Prestarea serviciilor de încredere calificate prin oficiile ASP

text_en: 36. Also, the EVOSign service, launched in pilot mode on 8 August 2024, has shown remarkable potential for rapid adoption.
summary: The EVOSign service was launched in pilot mode on 8 August 2024.
extraction_note: Pilot status: in_progress. STISC disputes that EVOSign is launched (consultation synthesis, pages 84 and 112); extracted there.
intervention_as_stated: Serviciul EVOSign

text_en: In just a few months after launch, the service attracted 15,450 users who completed registration and enabled 138,700 successful authentication sessions.
summary: EVOSign attracted 15,450 registered users and 138,700 successful authentications within months of launch.
extraction_note: Contradicts STISC's figures for the pilot to mid-December 2024 (8,583 users, 58,065 sessions; page 84), extracted separately. The next sentence (interest in intuitive authentication) is not extracted.

text_en: For EVOSign to become a truly transformative solution, it must be extended and improved to function as a digital identity wallet in line with the rigorous standards of the European Union. This involves integrating qualified electronic signature functions and implementing remote identification and registration mechanisms for users. Alignment with the European digital wallet model (EUDI Wallet) would position the country in line with European digital trends and stimulate the adoption of digital identity without requiring considerable financial investment in services at risk of low use.
summary: EVOSign is to be extended into an EU-standard digital identity wallet with qualified signatures and remote identification, aligned with the EUDI Wallet.
extraction_note: Same aim as action 4.1.3 of the Action Plan (page 60), extracted there as an action.
intervention_as_stated: Serviciul EVOSign

text_en: 37. According to the survey carried out by the EU-funded Moldova cybersecurity rapid assistance project, although 61% of respondents are confident they have good or very good knowledge of online safety, there is a significant gap: only 19% know what phishing is and 27% understand the concept of cyberbullying.
summary: EU-funded survey: 61% think they know online safety well, but only 19% know what phishing is.
extraction_note: Population cyber hygiene awareness; doubtful whether it meets the materiality test for the security of networks and information systems. The following sentence (need for information on cyber hygiene, pages 10-11) is not extracted.

text_en: 38. Despite efforts to strengthen cybersecurity, through creating the regulatory and institutional framework, primarily by creating the Cyber Security Agency, the number of cyberattacks in Moldova has increased significantly, by over 30% in the last three years.
summary: Despite the new Cyber Security Agency, cyberattacks in Moldova rose by over 30% in the last three years.
extraction_note: The Notă de fundamentare (page 68) states the period as 2021 to 2023 and speaks of incidents; extracted there.

text_en: This alarming trend underlines the urgent need to intensify investment in cybersecurity and adopt more effective measures to protect critical infrastructure and citizens' personal data.
summary: Rising cyberattacks show an urgent need for more cybersecurity investment to protect critical infrastructure and personal data.

text_en: 45. The level of local market adoption of IT products and services developed by resident companies, in other sectors of the national economy, is relatively low compared with the sector's overall growth.
summary: Other sectors of the economy adopt locally developed IT products and services relatively little.
extraction_note: Digitalisation of the wider economy (TECH-DIGI) rather than IT sector development; doubtful. The rest of the paragraph (sales and export figures) concerns the IT sector and is not extracted.

text_en: In recent years there has also been a significant increase in the number of foreign employees, a tenfold increase in 2023 compared with 2018.
summary: Foreign employees in Moldova's ICT sector increased tenfold between 2018 and 2023.
extraction_note: Foreign workers in Moldova fall within the Chapter 2 boundary in the run record; the paragraph concerns employment in the ICT sector. Chapter and cluster left empty because the passage names no accession chapter (brief). Analyst to confirm the Chapter 2 basis.

text_en: 47. Although the first e-commerce regulations in Moldova date from 2004, the sector's development has been slow, lacking a coordinated effort by the authorities and consistent market demand.
summary: E-commerce in Moldova developed slowly after its first regulation in 2004, lacking coordinated public effort and demand.

text_en: Only in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic was more attention paid to e-commerce, and the authorities, together with the private sector and with USAID support, drew up a Roadmap to stimulate the sector's development, on the basis of which a series of substantial amendments to the relevant legislation were promoted.
summary: With USAID support, authorities drew up an e-commerce Roadmap after COVID-19 and promoted substantial legislative amendments.
intervention_as_stated: Foaia de parcurs pentru dezvoltarea comerțului electronic

text_en: 48. The eCommerce report for Moldova 'Recommendations for eCommerce harmonisation with the EU' of March 2024 records significant progress by the Republic of Moldova in improving its e-commerce ecosystem, applying digital marketing strategies similar to those of the EU, thus laying the foundations for successful integration into the largest online markets.
summary: A March 2024 report on e-commerce harmonisation with the EU records significant progress in Moldova's e-commerce ecosystem.
extraction_note: The report's open challenges on payment on delivery (digital finance), returns and paper customs declarations (customs) and cross-border delivery are not extracted (R22).

text_en: 2) Unjustified blocking or limiting of a customer's access to the trader's online interface, which is planned to be resolved by alignment with Regulation (EU) 2018/302 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 February 2018 on addressing unjustified geo-blocking and other forms of discrimination based on customers' nationality, place of residence or place of establishment within the internal market, amending Regulations (EC) No 2006/2004 and (EU) 2017/2394 and Directive 2009/22/EC.
summary: An open e-commerce challenge is unjustified geo-blocking, to be addressed by aligning with the EU Geo-blocking Regulation 2018/302.
extraction_note: The same sentence states a planned alignment with Regulation (EU) 2018/302; the alignment appears as action 3.2.6 of the Action Plan (page 59) and is extracted there.

text_en: 50. At the end of 2023, 1,199 e-commerce platforms were registered, an increase of 57% compared with 2022.
summary: 1,199 e-commerce platforms were registered at end-2023, up 57% on 2022.
extraction_note: Also at page 69 (Notă de fundamentare), not extracted again.

text_en: According to the National Bank of Moldova, the value of online payments on e-commerce platforms in 2023 was about EUR 500 million, of which EUR 365 million purchases on foreign platforms and EUR 135 million on local platforms.
summary: Online payments on e-commerce platforms were about EUR 500 million in 2023, EUR 135 million of it on local platforms.
extraction_note: An e-commerce volume measured through payments; doubtful in view of the digital finance exclusion (R22).

text_en: Sales of tangible products and commercial services through e-commerce in Moldova, including cash on delivery, grew by 15.2% on the previous year, reaching an estimated EUR 358.6 million (excluding VAT) in 2023.
summary: E-commerce sales in Moldova grew 15.2% to an estimated EUR 358.6 million in 2023.

text_en: Overall, there is a visible digital divide in the market, with about 80% of the adult population excluded from e-commerce and the modern economy.
summary: About 80% of the adult population is excluded from e-commerce and the modern economy.
extraction_note: Also at page 69 (Notă de fundamentare), not extracted again. The sentence on customs procedures for online exports (same paragraph) is out of scope (R22).

text_en: 54. E-commerce development is also constrained by SMEs' slow adoption of digital technologies. Lack of knowledge, high costs of implementing digital solutions and a return perceived as long term discourage many SMEs from improving their online presence.
summary: Slow SME adoption of digital technologies, due to lack of knowledge, high costs and slow returns, constrains e-commerce.
extraction_note: Paragraphs 51-53 (cashless payments, digital financial inclusion, fintech) are out of scope as digital finance (R22).

text_en: 55. Currently, more than 60% of G2B public services are available electronically. About 2.5 out of 3 entrepreneurs prefer to use online services, and 5,392 entities use electronic invoicing.
summary: Over 60% of business public services are available electronically; 5,392 entities use e-invoicing.

text_en: 56. Since 2022, the Public Services Agency (ASP) has been obliged to register companies online, but owing to delays in developing internal information resources, this is done for the time being by e-mail.
summary: ASP must register companies online since 2022, but because of delays in its systems this is done by e-mail.

text_en: The electronic service 'Remote state registration of the legal unit' using the e-mail address is provisional and is to be provided during the time needed to develop and implement the new information system 'State Register of Legal Units', whose architecture provides for a dedicated software module for online state registration of legal units, conceived as a digital platform.
summary: Remote registration by e-mail is provisional until the new State Register of Legal Units provides an online registration platform.
extraction_note: The new system is described as still to be developed; ASP's view in the synthesis (page 129) gives development and launch dates.
intervention_as_stated: Sistemul informațional „Registrul de Stat al Unităților de Drept”

text_en: From 15 May 2023 to 30 September 2024, ASP processed 6,841 applications for online registration of legal entities.
summary: ASP processed 6,841 online legal entity registration applications between May 2023 and September 2024.

text_en: 59. 343 providers of electronic communications networks and services are authorised in the Republic of Moldova, with sales in 2023 of about MDL 6.35 billion, or 2.1% of GDP.
summary: 343 authorised electronic communications providers had 2023 sales of about MDL 6.35 billion, 2.1% of GDP.

text_en: The electronic communications sector shows relatively positive dynamics, with MDL 323.0 million of investment in 2023, an increase of 28.3% on the previous year.
summary: Electronic communications investment was MDL 323.0 million in 2023, up 28.3%.
extraction_note: Mostly in mobile and fixed networks (97.8%), per the next sentence.

text_en: 60. Since 1 January 2024, roaming tariffs between the Republic of Moldova and EU Member States have been reduced thanks to an agreement signed between the EU and our country. Mobile operators in the Republic of Moldova and those in the European Union and the European Economic Area voluntarily agreed to offer end users more advantageous offers.
summary: Since 1 January 2024, Moldova-EU roaming tariffs are reduced under an EU-Moldova agreement and voluntary operator offers.
intervention_as_stated: Acord UE-Republica Moldova privind tarifele de roaming

text_en: The current agreement is a short-term solution, based on voluntary arrangements between operators.
summary: The current roaming arrangement is a short-term solution based on voluntary operator agreements.

text_en: In this regard, following the adoption of Law No. 48/2023 on cybersecurity, the Cyber Security Agency was established, which acts as the national cybersecurity incident response team (CERT) and national single point of contact, and will ensure the implementation of state policy, supervision and control in the field of cybersecurity.
summary: Following Law 48/2023 on cybersecurity, the Cyber Security Agency was set up as national CERT and single point of contact.
extraction_note: M2: the establishment of the Agency is the intervention; its functions are stated in the same sentence. The Agency's full operationalisation is action 5.1.2 of the Action Plan.
intervention_as_stated: Agenția pentru Securitatea Cibernetică (Legea nr.48/2023 privind securitatea cibernetică)

text_en: 62. The Network Readiness Index 2023 report places the Republic of Moldova 67th of 134 countries assessed on network readiness indicators.
summary: Network Readiness Index 2023: Moldova 67th of 134 countries.
extraction_note: Also at page 70 (Notă de fundamentare), not extracted again.

text_en: Disaggregated data from this analysis show that our country performs best on population coverage by broadband networks, ranking 28th, network connection (FTTH/building internet subscriptions), 44th, device prices, 47th, internet service security, 48th, while the ICT regulatory framework is rated fairly easy, placing our country 34th.
summary: NRI 2023: Moldova's best ranks are broadband coverage (28th), FTTH subscriptions (44th) and ICT regulatory framework (34th).

text_en: 63. From another point of view, this international study identifies the weaknesses of the Republic of Moldova in readiness for the requirements of using the global network, namely: eCommerce legislation, 87th; investment in emerging technologies, 119th; global investment in electronic communications services, 108th; investment in R&D and universities, 86th; exports of products and services embedding advanced technologies (except ICT), 94th; digital payments in rural regions, 93rd; software spending, 93rd; privacy protection, 109th.
summary: NRI 2023 weaknesses include eCommerce legislation (87th), emerging technology investment (119th) and privacy protection (109th).

text_en: 64. The Republic of Moldova has evolved enormously in implementing advanced models of electronic communications market regulation, which has contributed greatly to the sector's development, according to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), but new measures are needed to adjust the institutional framework for policy development and market regulation mechanisms.
summary: ITU: Moldova advanced electronic communications market regulation, but the institutional framework for policy and regulation needs adjustment.

text_en: The ITU finds insufficient independence and accountability of the regulatory authority, and digital economy development policies must emphasise digital competitiveness, which can be significantly improved by using collaborative regulation tools, pro-competitive reforms in all areas related to digital transformation, regulatory incentives for innovation, and solid, enforceable mechanisms for consumer protection in the digital age.
summary: ITU finds the regulator insufficiently independent and accountable.
extraction_note: The same sentence also states what digital economy policies should emphasise; extracted as a separate recommendation item with the same quote.

text_en: The ITU finds insufficient independence and accountability of the regulatory authority, and digital economy development policies must emphasise digital competitiveness, which can be significantly improved by using collaborative regulation tools, pro-competitive reforms in all areas related to digital transformation, regulatory incentives for innovation, and solid, enforceable mechanisms for consumer protection in the digital age.
summary: Digital economy policies should stress competitiveness through collaborative regulation, pro-competitive reforms, innovation incentives and digital consumer protection.
extraction_note: Shares its quote with the finding on regulator independence (two claims of different types in one sentence).

text_en: Another important aspect concerns the lack of a single framework for managing and monitoring the implementation of digital economy and ICT sector development policies.
summary: There is no single framework for managing and monitoring digital economy and ICT sector policy implementation.

extraction_note: AGE's ground for deleting an indicator on services available through EVO; MDED accepted. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: integrarea Portalului guvernamental al serviciilor publice cu aplicația EVO

text_en: in AGE's opinion, the 2027 target is far too optimistic, considering that, apart from banks and insurance companies, the number of companies that might need to adopt e-KYC is very limited.
summary: AGE: the 2027 eKYC adoption target was too optimistic, as few companies beyond banks and insurers need eKYC.
extraction_note: On the indicator of entities adopting eKYC (Table 10, now a target of more than 20); MDED accepted the target of 20. Related to action 4.1.1 (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0213). Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: In this context, we inform that AGE has already started work on drafting such standards.
summary: AGE: it has already started drafting design standards for government platforms.
extraction_note: "Such standards" are the design standards applicable to government platforms named in the preceding sentence. Related to action 1.1.12 (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0197) and barrier -0100. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: standarde naționale de design pentru platformele guvernamentale

text_en: under Government Decision No. 1028/2023, the competent authority in the field of cybersecurity is exclusively the Cyber Security Agency.
summary: AGE: under Government Decision 1028/2023 the Cyber Security Agency is the sole competent cybersecurity authority.
extraction_note: M2: designation of a named institution. Related to MDA-GOV-2025-003-0066 (Law 48/2023). Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 1028/2023 (desemnarea Agenției pentru Securitate Cibernetică ca autoritate competentă)

text_en: We propose that Action 1.1.8 be excluded at this stage of the Programme's implementation because of the scalability risks of the EVO application.
summary: AGE: an EVO-related action should be dropped for now because of the EVO application's scalability risks.
extraction_note: Numbering of the February 2025 draft: action 1.1.8 there is not the eSocial action of the tabled plan (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0194); MDED accepted the removal. The claim is the scalability risk of EVO. Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: public authorities and institutions are obliged to use exclusively the government electronic notification service (MNotify) to collect recipients' contact data for sending electronic notifications and to notify them instead of on paper, unless the law provides otherwise, and are prohibited from creating and using services similar to MNotify.
summary: AGE: Government Decision 376/2020 obliges public bodies to use only MNotify for electronic notifications and bans similar services.
extraction_note: AGE's ground for deleting the earlier action 4.1.6 (official electronic address); MDED accepted, so the tabled 4.1.6 is a different action (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0217). Runs over the page break. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 376/2020 (serviciul guvernamental de notificare electronică MNotify)

text_en: The State Register of administrative-territorial units and addresses was partly optimised in 2024 with own resources, and its optimisation will continue under the internal project integrating it with the Real Estate Register.
summary: AGCC: the State Register of administrative units and addresses was partly optimised in 2024; integration with the Real Estate Register continues.
extraction_note: AGCC's ground for removing this register from action 5.2.1 (priority state registers, MDA-GOV-2025-003-0231); MDED accepted. Register modernisation is a material example of TECH-DATA, but this is a sector register; flagged. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: optimizarea Registrului de stat al unităților administrativ-teritoriale și al adreselor și integrarea cu Registrul bunurilor imobile

text_en: In Chapter X on the Action Plan, we propose adding to Specific Objective 1.1 a further point with the following action: "Development of electronic services for authenticated persons to submit electronic documents for cadastral registration in the real estate register".
summary: AGCC: add an action developing e-services for authenticated persons to submit documents for cadastral registration.
extraction_note: MDED rejected it as a sectoral action for the entity's own plan, with no financing identified. The first pass left cadastre proposals out as sectoral; land registry e-services used by the public are TECH-DGOV under rules section 4, so it is extracted and flagged for the analyst. The geoportal proposals on pages 124-125 remain out. Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: Thus, regarding cadastre, under Chapter 23 - Fundamental rights, an action to digitalise cadastral services is planned. It is not limited to clients submitting applications electronically, but also covers digitalising the execution of these services by modernising the Real Estate Register and implementing a new information system.
summary: AGCC: the National Accession Programme (Chapter 23) plans digitalising cadastral services, including online applications and a new Real Estate Register system.
extraction_note: Refers to the National Accession Programme 2025-2029 named in the preceding sentence. Chapter 23 is the PNA chapter, not this document's structure, so cluster and chapter are left empty. Online cadastral applications are TECH-DGOV; the back-office part is not. MDED replied that the Programme already has an objective on access to e-services. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: acțiunea de digitalizare a serviciilor cadastrale (Programul Național de Aderare 2025-2029, capitolul 23)

text_en: The RSUD information system will be built for all legal forms of organisation and most basic public services for submitting applications will be digitalised, namely:
summary: ASP: the new State Register of Legal Units will cover all legal forms and digitalise most basic application services.
extraction_note: The list that follows: registration, modification, suspension and resumption, deregistration, extracts, public utility status, percentage designation, name checks and reservation, and provisional registration of economic agents from the Transnistrian region (LIM-0044: recorded as stated, not used to judge performance there). Related to MDA-GOV-2025-003-0272 and -0273. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: Sistemul informațional „Registrul de stat al unităților de drept” (SI RSUD ver.2)

text_en: At the same time, the authority responsible for issuing and recording the qualified electronic signature certificates on the identity card is STISC;
summary: ASP: STISC is responsible for issuing and recording the qualified signature certificates on the new identity card.
extraction_note: M2: a statement of what an institution does, so a finding. Follows MDA-GOV-2025-003-0275. Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: At the same time, we reiterate that EvoSign is at the piloting and testing stage and does not hold the confirmations needed for use in electronic systems and services.
summary: STISC: EvoSign is still piloting and lacks the confirmations needed for use in electronic systems and services.
extraction_note: Adds to STISC's pilot-stage claim (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0252) that EvoSign lacks the confirmations for use in e-services; wording differs, so extracted (M3). Contradicts MDED (-0041, and the launch claim added at this check). Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: we propose revising the words "minimum security requirements" in the light of the draft Government Decision on implementing network and information system security measures by service providers in critical sectors (unique number 49/MDED/2025).
summary: STISC cites a draft Government Decision on network and information system security measures for critical-sector providers (49/MDED/2025).
extraction_note: The claim recorded is the existence of the draft decision (proposed); the sentence itself is a drafting proposal on the indicator of government IT systems meeting security measures, which MDED accepted. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: proiectul Hotărârii Guvernului cu privire la modul de implementare a măsurilor de securitate a rețelelor și sistemelor informatice de către furnizorii de servicii în sectoarele critice (număr unic 49/MDED/2025)

text_en: This aspect is also connected with the low level of knowledge of cyber hygiene rules.
summary: Low digital literacy is linked to low knowledge of cyber hygiene rules.
extraction_note: Notă de fundamentare; follows the 40.5% figure (MDA-GOV-2025-003-0237). Differs in wording from the Programme's para. 37 (added at this check), so extracted (M3). Doubtful as for that item. Added at the second-pass check.

text_en: The estimated state budget costs are planned for the actions harmonising and transposing the legislation of the Republic of Moldova with European Union requirements
summary: State budget costs of the Programme are planned for actions harmonising and transposing Moldovan law with EU requirements.
extraction_note: Notă de fundamentare. A statement on how the Programme is financed; recorded as a proposed intervention, could be read as a finding. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: finanțarea din bugetul de stat a acțiunilor de armonizare și transpunere a legislației UE din Program

text_en: 2.2.1. Drafting the Law on creating technology sandboxes to support innovation and entrepreneurial activity in emerging technologies
summary: Action 2.2.1: draft a law creating technology sandboxes for innovation and entrepreneurship in emerging technologies.
extraction_note: Action 2.2.1 of the Action Plan; deadline: Q3 2026; responsible/partners: MDED; other organisations and business associations; estimated cost: MDL 207.99 thousand (institution budget, development partners); monitoring indicator: draft law approved by the Government and sent to Parliament. The first pass left it out as an ICT sector action; the regulatory sandbox measure in the rationale of Objective 3.2 was extracted as MDA-GOV-2025-003-0141 (theme_doubtful), so this action is extracted on the same basis for the analyst to decide. Added at the second-pass check.
intervention_as_stated: proiectul de Lege cu privire la crearea de sandboxuri tehnologice
